Tooltip_item_RR_ModelManual_GP7:
The builder's operating manual for one class of locomotive:
controls, starting, running, what to do when she will not.
Read it and you can run a GP7 light engine.
Tooltip_item_RR_TrainHandlingBook:
The company book: the automatic brake, slack, grades, signals.
The brake handle you already know stops the locomotive and
nothing else. A train is stopped down the brake pipe, and
getting that wrong is what runs a grade away from you.
Long enough to take several sittings.
Teaches working a train: coupling cars and pulling them.
Without it a locomotive with cars on will not take power.
Tooltip_Recipe_RR_Operate_GP7: You can start and drive a GP7 light engine.
Tooltip_Recipe_RR_TrainHandling: You can couple cars and handle a train on the automatic brake.
Tooltip_item_RR_RailFrog: A steel ramp clamped over the railhead that a derailed wheel is driven back up into gauge.
Tooltip_item_RR_TrackJack: A thirty-ton ratchet jack for lifting a derailed truck and walking it back over the rails.
Tooltip_item_RR_RailSkate: A steel wedge over the railhead that holds the locomotive where she stands.
Tooltip_item_RR_SpikeMaul: A long-handled hammer with a narrow double face, for driving track spikes. A sledgehammer will do the job, but this is what it is for.
